sources.citation: Crosby & Stelovsky, How do we read algorithms? A case study, IEEE Computer 23(1), 1990
sources.shows: Programmers at two experience levels read a Pascal algorithm with many fixations and long dwell on relevant areas; viewing strategy differs from prose.
sources.doesNotShow: Any effect of presentation; small sample; 1990 display.

sources.citation: Busjahn et al., Eye movements in code reading: relaxing the linear order, ICPC 2015
sources.shows: Novices read code less linearly than prose; experts less linearly than novices.
sources.doesNotShow: Which layout helps; short Java snippets.

sources.citation: Peitek, Siegmund & Apel, What drives the reading order of programmers?, ICPC 2020
sources.shows: 12 novices and 19 intermediates; re-ran Busjahn et al. and Peacock et al.; linearity of code had an even stronger effect on reading order than experience.
sources.doesNotShow: Design implications; snippets only; effect of comprehension strategy not verified.

sources.citation: Uwano et al., Analyzing individual performance of source code review using reviewers' eye movement, ETRA 2006
sources.shows: Five reviewers, six 12-23 line C programs: 72.8% of lines seen in first 30% of time; short first sweeps went with slower defect finding.

sources.citation: Sharif, Falcone & Maletic, An eye-tracking study on the role of scan time in finding source code defects, ETRA 2012
sources.shows: Partial replication of Uwano: scan time correlates with defect-detection time and effort on defect lines.

sources.citation: Rodeghero et al., Improving automated source code summarization via an eye-tracking study of programmers, ICSE 2014
sources.shows: Ten professional Java programmers summarising methods; usually cited for signature focus (as restated by Abid et al.; not read directly).
sources.doesNotShow: Signature claim only as restated by Abid; contested (not like-for-like replicated) by Abid 2019 under different conditions.

sources.citation: Abid et al., Developer reading behavior while summarizing Java methods: size and context matters, ICSE 2019
sources.shows: 18 developers, 63 methods in Eclipse: more gaze on method body than signature; revisit control-flow terms; long gaze on call terms.
sources.doesNotShow: Any presentation effect; summarisation task only.

sources.citation: Xia et al., Measuring program comprehension: a large-scale field study with professionals, IEEE TSE 44(10), 2018
sources.shows: Field instrumentation of 78 professionals on 7 projects, 3,148 hours: about 58% of time is program-comprehension activity.
sources.doesNotShow: Reading behaviour; anything about documents; comprehension is inferred from activity classes.

sources.citation: Ko, Myers, Coblenz & Aung, An exploratory study of how developers seek, relate, and collect relevant information, IEEE TSE 32(12), 2006
sources.shows: Developers searched with limited, misleading cues, then followed dependencies.

sources.citation: Lawrance et al., How programmers debug, revisited: an information foraging theory perspective, IEEE TSE 39(2), 2013
sources.shows: Navigation while debugging modelled as scent-following; ten professionals.

sources.citation: Obaidellah, Al Haek & Cheng, A survey on the usage of eye-tracking in computer programming, ACM CSUR 51(1), 2018
sources.shows: Survey of eye tracking in programming research.

sources.citation: Brown, Kölling & Weill-Tessier, An eye tracking study assessing the impact of background styling in code editors on novice programmers' code understanding, ICER 2023
sources.depth: abstract only (KCL research portal; ACM page 403)
sources.shows: Plain Java vs BlueJ scope highlighting vs Stride, 62 novices (count from search summary): gaze differed, correctness and speed did not.

sources.citation: Duggan & Payne, Skim reading by satisficing: evidence from eye tracking, CHI 2011
sources.shows: Skimmers direct attention to important content and move on when information gain drops.
sources.doesNotShow: Code, READMEs or transcripts; expository prose only; a re-analysis of the 2009 eye data, not an independent study.

sources.citation: Duggan & Payne, Text skimming: the process and effectiveness of foraging through text under time pressure, JEP:Applied 15(3), 2009
sources.shows: Vs reading half the text, skimming improved memory for important ideas, not details or inferences; no advantage over reading first/second half of each paragraph; benefit depended on navigability in web-like layouts.

sources.citation: Lorch, Text-signaling devices and their effects on reading and memory processes, Educ. Psychol. Rev. 1(3), 1989
sources.shows: Review: most signals improve memory for cued information; unsignalled information often unaffected.
sources.doesNotShow: Speed of locating; effects on attention; non-prose.

sources.citation: Nielsen, F-shaped pattern for reading web content, Nielsen Norman Group, 2006
sources.shows: 232 users, eye tracking of web pages: rough F-shaped scan; author notes E and L variants.
sources.doesNotShow: Peer review; documents, READMEs or code.

sources.citation: Barke, James & Polikarpova, Grounded Copilot, OOPSLA 2023 (arXiv 2206.15000)
sources.shows: 20 programmers; acceleration vs exploration modes with Copilot.
sources.doesNotShow: How finished output is read or verified.

sources.citation: Vaithilingam, Zhang & Glassman, Expectation vs. experience, CHI EA 2022
sources.shows: 24 participants: Copilot did not necessarily improve time or success; most preferred it.

sources.citation: Mozannar, Bansal, Fourney & Horvitz, Reading between the lines, CHI 2024 (arXiv 2210.14306)
sources.shows: 21 programmers; CUPS taxonomy of activities and their time costs.
sources.doesNotShow: Per-activity numbers not verified; none used.

sources.citation: Liang, Yang & Myers, A large-scale survey on the usability of AI programming assistants, ICSE 2024 (arXiv 2303.17125)
sources.shows: 410 developers: outputs failing requirements and difficulty steering are main barriers.

sources.citation: Epperson et al., Interactive debugging and steering of multi-agent AI systems, CHI 2025 (arXiv 2503.02068)
sources.shows: Five developer interviews: reviewing long agent conversations to localise errors is hard; 14-participant test of an editing/reset tool.

sources.citation: Duma et al., These aren't the reviews you're looking for, EASE 2026 (arXiv 2605.02273)
sources.shows: AIDev dataset: abstract says most AI-generated PRs receive no review; review more often automation-mediated; review metrics may mislead. No percentage or definition in the abstract.

sources.citation: Bacchelli & Bird, Expectations, outcomes, and challenges of modern code review, ICSE 2013
sources.shows: Review at Microsoft is less about defects than expected; knowledge transfer and awareness matter.

sources.citation: Schroeter (Schröter), Bettenburg & Premraj, Do stack traces help developers fix bugs?, MSR 2010
sources.shows: Evidence that developers use stack traces when debugging Eclipse bugs.
sources.doesNotShow: Whether line numbers or any display aid helps.

sources.citation: Yuan, Park & Zhou, Characterizing logging practices in open-source software, ICSE 2012
sources.shows: How developers write and revise log statements in four systems.

sources.citation: He et al., A survey on automated log analysis for reliability engineering, ACM CSUR 54(6), 2021
sources.shows: Survey of automated log parsing, compression and analysis.
sources.doesNotShow: Anything about human reading of logs.

sources.citation: Barik et al., Do developers read compiler error messages?, ICSE 2017
sources.depth: abstract only (search result quoting the ACM page); secondary summary agrees
sources.shows: 56 undergraduate/graduate students in Eclipse: 13-25% of task time reading error messages; difficulty predicts performance.
sources.doesNotShow: Logs generally; the MSR 2016 Barik lead could not be verified and is dropped.

sources.citation: Baltes & Diehl, Usage and attribution of Stack Overflow code snippets in GitHub projects, EMSE 2019
sources.shows: Copying snippets from Stack Overflow into GitHub projects is common and rarely properly attributed.

sources.citation: Yang, Martins, Saini & Lopes, Stack Overflow in GitHub: any snippets there?, MSR 2017
sources.shows: Asks whether snippets are found in projects and whether copies are literal or adapted.

spec.default: Mod+C in Rendered mode resolves the selection through provenance to source bytes; never DOM text
spec.why: Follows from commitment 4; en-dash/curly-quote substitution is an engineering fact, its frequency unmeasured.
spec.marxyToday: partly contradicted - drag selections copy getSelection().toString() (apps/desktop/src/selection/view.ts, apply.ts); click-selected nodes run copy-code-clean / copy-section from the buffer first

spec.default: on in Source mode; none in Rendered gutter
spec.why: Shared coordinate with compilers, traces and reviews; no study of retrieval benefit.
spec.marxyToday: contradicted - apps/desktop/src/app.ts:117 passes lineNumbers: false (wrapper default is on)

spec.default: said / run / returned distinguishable at a glance; nothing collapsed by default
spec.why: AGDebugger names the problem; no test of a design.
spec.marxyToday: open - fences distinguished only by info string; details renders open (sanitiser policy)

spec.default: +/- marker is primary cue; colour secondary with shape/weight difference
spec.why: Colour alone excludes some readers; no reading-task test.
spec.marxyToday: open - markup.inserted/deleted map to no class (packages/core/src/highlight/scopes.ts)

spec.default: clear heading hierarchy, informative first lines, summoned outline, no per-section chrome
spec.why: Lorch and Duggan & Payne are prose studies (both [C]); no test on READMEs or transcripts.
spec.marxyToday: applied - outline and heading type scale exist

operations.title: Copy selection as source text (provenance-resolved)
operations.why: Replaces DOM-text copy so smart typography cannot reach the clipboard.

operations.title: Copy shell command without prompts
operations.why: Strips a leading prompt only when every non-blank line has one; reader's choice, never automatic.

operations.title: Extract every fenced block
operations.why: Lifts the commands a transcript ran into one paste.

operations.title: Extract open tasks
operations.why: Answers what is left in a plan without reading it.

operations.title: Copy path:line for the selection
operations.why: A working retrieval cue for agents, reviews and traces; uses the buffer line index.

operations.title: Copy the new side of a diff

gaps.what: Copy that bypasses smartened DOM text
gaps.detail: Copy-as-plain-text is a v1.1 candidate; the frozen operation contract has no selection-copy that resolves through provenance by default.
gaps.proposal: An ADR admitting a default provenance-resolved copy, or amending copy behaviour in apps/desktop/src/selection without a contract change.

gaps.detail: markup.inserted/deleted map to no token class; adding one needs the twelve-class contract to change.
gaps.proposal: An ADR adding one or two diff classes.

gaps.what: Distinguishing command from result in transcripts
gaps.detail: Info strings are the only cue; details/summary are transparent so authored collapsing is lost.
gaps.proposal: Decide whether an info-string convention is enough or a registry entry is needed.

gaps.what: No evidence that any presentation aids verification of agent output
gaps.detail: No study; Marxy cannot collect telemetry.
gaps.proposal: Treat designs as [D] and fail safe; run a taste review.

stories.summary: Copy exactly what the source says from Rendered mode
stories.why: Prose --frozen-lockfile copies as an en dash today.
acceptance: 1. A new test in apps/desktop/src/selection asserts Mod+C over a rendered selection yields the source bytes for the range.

stories.summary: Show line numbers in Source mode by default
stories.why: Line numbers are the shared coordinate for traces and reviews.
acceptance: 1. A unit test on createSourceEditor asserts the line-number extension is present by default.
stories.tasteRow: Before/after Source mode screenshots; is the gutter too heavy at rest?

stories.why: Retrieval cue for agents and reviewers.
acceptance: 1. A new operations test covers copy-line-reference on a CRLF buffer.

taste: Whether command and result should look different in a transcript.
Whether line-number gutters in Source mode are too heavy at rest.
Whether an open <details> in a transcript helps or hurts skimming.
changeMyMind: A controlled study showing collapsed tool output improves error-catching would reverse the no-collapse default.
A measured frequency of copy-substitution errors near zero would lower the priority of provenance-resolved copy.
A study showing line numbers do not aid retrieval would drop the Source-mode default.
